title: L1: Reduce SVD of A to explicit Gram matrix (1-t^i)/i

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Goal.** Reduce the singular-value problem for $A=B^{(H)}\circ J$ to an explicit infinite Gram matrix.

Show $A^*e_i=J^*(B^{(H)})^*e_i$ with $(B^{(H)})^*e_i=t^{i-1}$, $[J^*g](t)=\int_t^1 g$, hence
$$[A^*e_i](t)=\int_t^1 s^{i-1}\,ds=\frac{1-t^{i}}{i}.$$
Deduce the entries of $AA^*$ on $\ell^2$:
$$(AA^*)_{ij}=\Big\langle\tfrac{1-t^i}{i},\tfrac{1-t^j}{j}\Big\rangle_{L^2(0,1)}=\frac{1}{ij}\Big(1-\frac1{i+1}-\frac1{j+1}+\frac1{i+j+1}\Big).\quad(\star)$$

Justify rigorously: (a) $\sigma_i(A)^2=\lambda_i(AA^*)$ (compactness of $A$, spectral theorem); (b) the infinite matrix $(\star)$ genuinely represents the compact self-adjoint operator $AA^*$ in the standard ONB $\{e_i\}$ of $\ell^2$ — e.g. verify $\sum_{i,j}(AA^*)_{ij}^2<\infty$ (Hilbert–Schmidt) so the matrix and operator coincide.

**Difficulty:** low–moderate. This is the algebraic foundation for all subsequent estimates; every later lemma analyzes the spectrum of $(\star)$.
